note: Authoritative contract events the automated AFLRATINGS feed missed or got wrong. events.note: Re-signed for a further two years to 2021 after a breakout 2018 season (24 games) that saw him finish runner-up in the Peter Crimmins Medal.

events.name: Blake Hardwick
events.note: Signed a new long-term deal to remain at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2024.

events.name: Blake Hardwick
events.note: Turned down free agency to sign a five-year contract extension, keeping him at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2029.

events.name: Justin McInerney
events.note: McInerney, then 21, signed a four-year contract extension keeping him at Sydney until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Justin McInerney
events.note: McInerney, then 25, signed a five-year extension taking his name off the free agency list and committing him to Sydney through the end of 2031.

events.name: Brayden Maynard
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension through to the end of the 2020 season.

events.name: Brayden Maynard
events.note: Turned down eligibility for free agency at end of 2022 to sign a three-year extension through to the end of 2025.

events.name: Brayden Maynard
events.note: As an unrestricted free agent, rejected interest from North Melbourne and other rivals to re-sign with Collingwood on a four-year deal through to the end of 2029.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Traded from Melbourne to Collingwood in a four-club, day-six 2015 trade period deal (Pies sent Paul Seedsman and Ben Kennedy the other way, along with pick 68, for Howe).

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.reporter: Collingwood FC (collingwoodfc.com.au), "Howe signs on for three"
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension with Collingwood, tying him to the club until the end of the 2021 season.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Added another year to his existing deal, locking him in at Collingwood until the end of 2022 (alongside Jamie Elliott).

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Signed a one-year extension on the eve of the 2023 season, committing him to Collingwood through the end of 2024.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Signed a one-year extension to play on in 2025, his 10th season at Collingwood.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.reporter: Collingwood FC (collingwoodfc.com.au), "Sidebottom and Howe sign on"
events.note: Signed a one-year extension (announced late August 2025) alongside Steele Sidebottom to play a 16th AFL season in 2026.

events.name: Jack Ginnivan
events.note: Ginnivan signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood, announced alongside teammates Nathan Kreuger/Ruscoe.

events.name: Jack Ginnivan
events.note: Ginnivan was traded from Collingwood to Hawthorn on the final day of the 2023 AFL Trade Period, with clubs swapping second-round picks and Collingwood also receiving a future third-round selection.

events.name: Jack Ginnivan
events.note: On joining Hawthorn via trade, Ginnivan signed a four-year deal, three years longer than what remained on his Collingwood contract; Hawthorn's own site lists him as contracted until 2027.

events.name: Sam Flanders
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Gold Coast, tying him to the club through the end of 2023.

events.name: Sam Flanders
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension with Gold Coast through to the end of 2027, announced live on stage at the club's Best Emerging Player award night.

events.name: Sam Flanders
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to St Kilda during the AFL Trade Period, with the Saints sending Pick 7 in the 2025 National Draft to the Suns; reported to have signed a new long-term deal with St Kilda as part of the move.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Western Bulldogs until at least the end of 2019.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Re-signed with the Western Bulldogs on a two-year extension, committing him to the club until at least the end of 2021.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Signed a two-year extension with the Western Bulldogs, taking him from a 2021 expiry to at least the end of 2023.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Recommitted to the Western Bulldogs on a four-year extension, keeping him at the club until at least the end of the 2027 season.

events.name: Beau McCreery
events.note: McCreery signed a three-year contract extension with Collingwood, announced alongside John Noble and Jakob Ryan re-signing, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027. Exact day of the announcement wasn't stated on the page (July 2023 per corroborating coverage), so the date is estimated to mid-month.

events.name: Tom De Koning
events.note: De Koning signed a two-year contract extension with Carlton, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2025, turning down rival interest.

events.name: Tom De Koning
events.note: De Koning left Carlton as a restricted free agent (Carlton chose not to match St Kilda's offer) and signed a reported eight-year deal with St Kilda, officially joining when free agency opened on 3 October 2025.

events.name: James Peatling
events.note: Peatling signed a two-year contract extension with GWS, tying him to the Giants until the end of 2024.

events.name: James Peatling
events.note: Traded from GWS to Adelaide on the final day of the 2024 AFL Trade Period; Adelaide sent a future second-round pick for Peatling plus future third- and fourth-round selections.

events.name: James Peatling
events.reporter: Tom Morris (Channel 9 / Trade Radio) via X
events.note: Alongside the trade, Peatling signed a four-year contract with Adelaide, running through the end of 2028.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Lobb signed a two-year contract extension with GWS, rejecting interest from WA clubs, keeping him at the Giants through the end of 2019.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Traded from GWS to Fremantle on the final day of the 2018 trade period (GWS received picks 11 and 19; Fremantle gave up Lobb plus picks 14, 43 and 47); Lobb signed a four-year deal running from 2019 to 2022.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to the Western Bulldogs (Bulldogs gave up pick 30 in the 2022 draft and a future second-round pick) and signed a four-year contract through to the end of 2026.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Lobb signed a further contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, adding a season and keeping him at the club through the end of 2027, amid career-best form as a key defender.

events.name: Jaspa Fletcher
events.note: Fletcher signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the club until the end of the 2026 season, after a strong debut 2023 campaign that included a Round 19 Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Jaspa Fletcher
events.note: Having already been contracted through 2026, Fletcher signed a further four-year extension with Brisbane, taking his deal through to the end of 2030, shortly after the club's 2025 premiership.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Hill signed a one-year contract extension with Hawthorn in September 2013, tying him to the club until the end of 2015.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: After an outstanding start to the 2014 season, Hawthorn re-signed Hill on a new deal locking him in until the end of 2017.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Traded from Hawthorn to Fremantle (Hawthorn received pick 23 in the 2016 NAB AFL Draft) so Hill could return to Western Australia and play alongside brother Stephen Hill.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: On joining Fremantle via trade from Hawthorn, Hill signed a five-year contract; a 2018 club article confirmed he was contracted at Fremantle until at least the end of the 2021 season.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to St Kilda on the final day of the 2019 Trade Period, with St Kilda sending Blake Acres, picks 10 and 58, and future selections to Fremantle for Hill.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Upon arriving at St Kilda via trade from Fremantle, Hill signed a five-year contract with the Saints.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.reporter: National Indigenous Times / Canberra Times / St Kilda FC
events.note: Ahead of his 250th AFL game, Hill signed a three-year contract extension with St Kilda, committing him to the club until at least the end of the 2027 season.

events.name: Mark Keane
events.note: After leaving Collingwood (delisted/uncontracted following a stint back in Ireland during Covid), Keane signed a one-year deal with Adelaide during the pre-season supplemental signing period.

events.name: Mark Keane
events.note: Keane turned down interest from Victorian clubs, including a return to former club Collingwood, and signed a three-year contract extension keeping him at Adelaide until at least the end of 2028.

events.name: Jack Buckley
events.note: Upgraded from Category B rookie to the primary list with a two-year contract after his 2020 AFL debut.

events.name: Jack Buckley
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension (the first multi-year deal of his career) to remain at GWS through the end of 2026, about eight weeks after returning from a serious knee injury.

events.name: Jack Buckley
events.note: Signed a new four-year contract extension, adding to his existing 2026 deal to commit to GWS through the end of the 2030 season.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir signed a three-year contract extension with Sydney, tying him to the club through the end of 2021; Head of Football Tom Harley confirmed the deal.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir requested a trade from Sydney to Port Adelaide, who sent a future second-round pick to the Swans; he signed a four-year deal at Port Adelaide as part of the move.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir signed a two-year contract extension with Port Adelaide, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir triggered a one-year contract extension ahead of the 2026 season, tying him to Port Adelaide until the end of 2027.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale was one of five young Cats to sign a contract extension, tying him to Geelong through the end of 2023.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale and James Willis recommitted to Geelong, with Neale signing a two-year extension to remain at the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale signed a three-year extension alongside Jeremy Cameron and Ollie Henry, committing to Geelong until at least the end of 2028.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale signed a two-year contract extension, committing to Geelong until at least the end of 2030; this is his current active deal.

events.name: Charlie Curnow
events.note: Curnow signed a four-year contract extension with Carlton, committing to the club until at least the end of 2023.

events.name: Charlie Curnow
events.note: Fresh off his first Coleman Medal, Curnow signed a six-year contract extension with Carlton, tying him to the club until the end of 2029, turning down a reported seven-year rival offer.

events.name: Charlie Curnow
events.note: Sydney won the race for Curnow on the final day of the 2025 trade period, sending Will Hayward and first-round picks in 2025, 2026 and 2027 to Carlton in return for the two-time Coleman Medallist plus picks 31, 42 and a 2027 second-round selection.

events.name: Connor Rozee
events.note: Rozee and teammate Zak Butters both signed two-year contract extensions with Port Adelaide, tying them to the club through to the end of the 2024 season.

events.name: Connor Rozee
events.reporter: Port Adelaide FC / ESPN AFL / Zero Hanger
events.note: Rozee was appointed Port Adelaide captain and signed an eight-year contract extension, the club's biggest-ever deal, committing him to the Power until the end of 2032.

events.name: Paul Curtis
events.note: Curtis signed a three-year contract extension with North Melbourne, committing to the club until at least the end of 2028; he was previously contracted through 2025.

events.name: Paul Curtis
events.note: Curtis signed a five-year extension keeping him at North Melbourne through at least 2033, having previously been committed until 2028; the club's head of football talent Brady Rawlings praised him as a key part of the Roos' young forward crop. Exact announcement date could not be confirmed from the source and was estimated to mid-2026.

events.name: Jake Soligo
events.note: Soligo, previously contracted through the end of 2025, signed a four-year contract extension with Adelaide keeping him at the club through the 2029 season.

events.name: Sam Switkowski
events.note: Signed a contract extension during the 2022 season (after recovering from a Round 13 back injury) keeping him at Fremantle through the end of 2024.

events.name: Sam Switkowski
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, adding to his previous 2024 deal and committing him to Fremantle through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Angus Sheldrick
events.note: Sheldrick signed a two-year contract extension with the Swans, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2025 (reported in a Sydney Swans article about Nick Blakey's own extension, which noted Sheldrick had 're-signed earlier this season').

events.name: Angus Sheldrick
events.note: Sheldrick agreed to a two-year contract extension keeping him at Sydney through the end of 2027, resisting interest from other clubs including West Coast, after establishing himself as a regular AFL midfielder.

events.name: Josh Battle
events.note: Battle, then 19, re-signed with St Kilda on a two-year deal after completing Year 12, his first re-signing since being drafted in 2016 (exact date not stated in source, estimated to mid-2018).

events.name: Josh Battle
events.note: Battle signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, securing him through the end of 2024; also reported by AFL.com.au ("Battle won: Defender re-signs") and saints.com.au ("Battle ready for future at Saints").

events.name: Josh Battle
events.note: Battle left St Kilda after eight seasons/123 games and joined Hawthorn as an unrestricted free agent on a six-year deal through the end of 2030; St Kilda received band-one free agency compensation (pick 8, 2024 draft).

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.note: Richmond delisted Chol at the end of the 2018 season; GM Neil Balme said the club would not offer him a new contract.

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.reporter: Wikipedia (citing Fox Sports rookie draft live coverage)
events.note: After being delisted, Chol was re-drafted by Richmond with pick 45 in the 2019 (Nov 2018) rookie draft, restarting his AFL career at the same club.

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.note: At the end of the 2021 season Chol exercised free agency and left Richmond to join Gold Coast; the Suns lodged free agent paperwork with the AFL.

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.note: With two years still to run on his Gold Coast contract, Chol requested a trade; Hawthorn acquired him (plus pick 62) for a future 2nd-round pick and signed him to a new four-year deal.

events.name: Darcy Wilmot
events.note: Wilmot, then contracted until end of 2025, signed a two-year extension (alongside Kai Lohmann) keeping him at Brisbane until at least the end of 2027; announced September 2023.

events.name: Darcy Wilmot
events.note: Wilmot, already contracted until end of 2027, signed a further two-year extension keeping him at Brisbane until at least the end of 2029; announced 8 December 2025.

events.name: Max Hall
events.note: Hall signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027, after breaking out as one of the surprise packets of the 2025 AFL season following his mid-season draft selection in 2024.

events.name: Will Ashcroft
events.note: Ashcroft signed a four-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the club through the end of 2030; the deal came after his second consecutive Norm Smith Medal and Brisbane's back-to-back premierships.

events.name: Harry Sheezel
events.note: Sheezel signed a four-year contract extension with North Melbourne, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2030; he had previously been contracted through 2026.

events.name: Harry Sheezel
events.note: North Melbourne vice-captain Sheezel added a further two years onto his previous deal, locking him in with the Kangaroos through the end of 2032.

events.name: Riley Thilthorpe
events.note: Thilthorpe, originally contracted through 2022 as the No.2 pick in the 2020 draft, signed a three-year contract extension with Adelaide, committing him to the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Riley Thilthorpe
events.note: Already contracted through 2025, Thilthorpe signed a further three-year extension with Adelaide, taking his deal through to the end of the 2028 season (when he will become a free agent).

events.name: Gryan Miers
events.note: Signed a new three-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026; announced on the eve of his 100th AFL game against Essendon.

events.name: Gryan Miers
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, committing to the club until at least the end of 2028; signed a year before he would have become a free agent.

events.name: Tom Atkins
events.note: Atkins signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027; he had been eligible for free agency at season's end but chose to re-sign.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: Traded from Sydney to Collingwood (with pick 62) in exchange for pick 56 during the 2019 trade period, after requesting a move to Victoria for more senior opportunity; joined the Magpies on a two-year contract.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: Signed a fresh three-year contract extension with Collingwood, committing him to the club through the end of 2025.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension alongside teammates Patrick Lipinski and Finlay Macrae, pushing his deal out to the end of 2026.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: With one year remaining on his existing deal (through 2026), signed a new three-year extension keeping him at Collingwood through the end of 2029; reportedly turned down interest from West Coast to re-sign.

events.name: Shaun Mannagh
events.note: Mannagh signed a contract extension with Geelong keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Shaun Mannagh
events.reporter: Geelong Cats (official) / Geelong Independent / Zero Hanger
events.note: Mannagh signed a three-year contract extension, keeping him at Geelong until the end of the 2029 season.

events.name: Jason Horne-Francis
events.note: Horne-Francis was traded from North Melbourne to Port Adelaide in a four-club mega trade (also involving West Coast and GWS), joining Port on a six-year deal running until the end of 2028.

events.name: Jason Horne-Francis
events.note: As part of his move, Horne-Francis signed a six-year contract with Port Adelaide, listed as contracted until the end of 2028; this remains his active deal as of mid-2026 with no confirmed further extension found (an April 2026 AFL.com.au video titled 'Port's pay rise, mega deal for Horne-Francis' hints at extension talk but no signed terms could be verified).

events.name: Jeremy Cameron
events.note: Cameron signed a five-year contract extension with GWS, keeping him at the club through to the end of 2020, heading off interest from Victorian clubs including Carlton.

events.name: Jeremy Cameron
events.note: After Cameron requested a move as a restricted free agent and Geelong's bid went unmatched, GWS traded him to the Cats on the final day of the 2020 trade period for a package of draft picks; he signed a five-year deal with Geelong.

events.name: Jeremy Cameron
events.note: Cameron signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027.

events.name: Josh Treacy
events.note: Treacy signed a three-year contract extension with Fremantle, committing through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Josh Treacy
events.note: Treacy signed a further four-year extension with Fremantle, taking his contract through to the end of the 2030 season, alongside forward teammates Luke Jackson and Jye Amiss also being re-signed long-term.

events.name: Oliver Dempsey
events.note: Dempsey signed a four-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at GMHBA Stadium through the end of 2029, off the back of his 2024 AFL Rising Star-winning season.

events.name: Kade Chandler
events.note: Chandler signed a three-year extension with Melbourne, committing him to the club through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Kade Chandler
events.note: Chandler turned down free agency and re-signed with Melbourne for a further five years, committing to the club until the end of 2031.

events.name: Josh Ward
events.note: Ward signed a two-year contract extension with Hawthorn, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2025, after a strong debut season and Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Josh Ward
events.note: Ward signed a four-year contract extension with Hawthorn, taking him through to free agency at the end of 2029.

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Traded from GWS to Carlton with less than an hour remaining in the 2017 AFL trade period, in exchange for selection 28; GWS had not offered him a new contract.

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Re-signed with Carlton on a new one-year deal, keeping him at the club through the end of 2022 (exact publication date not shown on page; dated via related SEN coverage from April 27, 2022).

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Extended his contract with Carlton for three more years, taking him through to the end of 2025, on the back of career-best form.

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Traded from Carlton to the Western Bulldogs in the dying minutes of the 2024 trade period, as part of a four-club, three-player deal also involving Bailey Smith (to Geelong) and Jack Macrae (to St Kilda); Carlton received pick 38. New contract length/end year with the Bulldogs was not publicly disclosed by either club.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2019 season.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Re-signed with the Western Bulldogs alongside Caleb Daniel for a further three years, locking him in until the end of 2022.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Traded from the Western Bulldogs to the Brisbane Lions on the final day of the 2022 AFL Trade Period, after requesting a move; the Bulldogs received a first, second and fourth-round future selection plus pick 21.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Signed a six-year contract with the Brisbane Lions on joining the club as part of the trade from the Western Bulldogs, running from the 2023 season.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, taking him to the end of 2030, following his first Merrett-Murray Medal (2025) and appointment as Lions co-captain for 2026.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: As club captain, Zorko re-signed with Brisbane to keep him contracted until the end of 2022.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Zorko, an unrestricted free agent, signed a one-year contract extension keeping him at Brisbane for a 12th season in 2023.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Signed a new one-year deal to play on for a 13th season in 2024, off the back of a Grand Final campaign.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Signed a one-year deal for a 14th season, keeping him at Brisbane through the end of 2025.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension ahead of his 300th AFL game, keeping him at Brisbane for a 15th season through 2026.

events.name: Jack Steele
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2022.

events.name: Jack Steele
events.note: Dual All-Australian and Saints co-captain signed a fresh five-year contract extension, committing to St Kilda until the end of 2027.

events.name: Jack Steele
events.note: Traded from St Kilda to Melbourne on deadline day of the AFL Trade Period for a future third-round selection; his contract was extended by an added year as part of the move, locking him in at the Demons until the end of 2028.

events.name: Joel Freijah
events.reporter: Western Bulldogs official website / Zero Hanger
events.note: As a first-year AFL player (drafted pick 45, 2023), Freijah signed a one-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, taking his deal through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Joel Freijah
events.note: Freijah signed a three-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2029 season; announced alongside teammate Rhylee West's own extension.

events.name: Bodhi Uwland
events.note: Uwland, a Gold Coast Academy graduate, signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Suns until the end of 2026, after a breakout 2024 season and a Round 12 Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Bodhi Uwland
events.note: Uwland signed a new long-term extension (reported as a four-year deal) keeping him at the Suns through to the end of 2030, alongside teammate Lachie Weller who extended to 2029.

events.name: Willem Drew
events.note: Drew re-signed a two-year contract extension with Port Adelaide, tying him to the club until the end of 2020.

events.name: Willem Drew
events.note: Drew signed a two-year contract extension, tying him to Port Adelaide until the end of 2022.

events.name: Willem Drew
events.note: As part of a quartet of Port Adelaide re-signings (with Houston, Clurey, Burton), Drew extended his contract by two years to the end of 2024.

events.name: Willem Drew
events.note: Drew signed a four-year contract extension, tying him to Port Adelaide through the end of 2028, taking him beyond his initial free agency eligibility.

events.name: Darcy Fort
events.note: Traded from Geelong to Brisbane on trade deadline day, with the Lions sending pick 50 and a future third-round selection to the Cats for Fort and pick 41.

events.name: Darcy Fort
events.note: Re-signed with Brisbane on a new two-year deal keeping him at the club through the end of 2025, despite interest from rival clubs.

events.name: Darcy Fort
events.note: Extended his stay at Brisbane by one year, signing on through the end of 2026 alongside premiership teammate Logan Morris.

events.name: Callum Wilkie
events.note: Wilkie signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, keeping him at the club through the end of 2023, after being named to the club's 2021 leadership group.

events.name: Callum Wilkie
events.note: Wilkie added a further one-year extension, taking his contract through to the end of 2024, alongside fellow defender Josh Allison.

events.name: Callum Wilkie
events.note: Wilkie re-signed with St Kilda until the end of 2027, alongside Jack Sinclair and Jack Higgins, with a year still to run on his existing deal at the time.

events.name: Callum Wilkie
events.reporter: Zero Hanger (via Callum Twomey/St Kilda CEO Carl Dilena)
events.note: St Kilda reworked Wilkie's deal amid Western Bulldogs interest, adding 'a couple more years' beyond its original 2027 end date; exact new end year not officially disclosed, estimated at 2029.

events.name: Jordan Clark
events.note: 18-year-old Clark signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, committing him to the club until the end of 2022.

events.name: Jordan Clark
events.note: Clark was traded from Geelong to Fremantle on the final day of the 2021 AFL Trade Period, with the Dockers sending pick 22 and a future third-round pick (via Carlton) to the Cats for Clark and a future fourth-round pick.

events.name: Jordan Clark
events.note: Clark signed a three-year contract extension with Fremantle, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2028 season; he was previously contracted only to the end of 2025.

events.name: Cam Rayner
events.note: Rayner signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, taking him through to the end of 2023, despite already being contracted for the following season.

events.name: Cam Rayner
events.note: After rupturing his ACL in a pre-season match and facing a season-ending injury, Rayner asked for a two-year extension (rather than the club's offered one year), pushing his deal to the end of 2025.

events.name: Cam Rayner
events.note: Coming off a career-best 2024 season (All-Australian squad selection, personal-best 31 goals) and set to be a prime 2025 free agent, Rayner rejected free agency and signed a six-year extension with Brisbane through to the end of 2031.

events.name: Josh Rachele
events.reporter: Theo Doropoulos (via X/Twitter), reported around Crows season launch address
events.note: Rachele signed a 2-year contract extension, keeping him at Adelaide until the end of 2025; announced by Crows chairman John Olsen during the club's season launch address.

events.name: Josh Rachele
events.note: Rachele signed a four-year extension, committing to Adelaide until at least the end of 2029; he had been contracted to 2025 prior to this deal.

events.name: Josh Daicos
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood after his 2018 season, alongside Brody Mihocek.

events.name: Josh Daicos
events.note: Re-signed with Collingwood for two more seasons following his breakout 2020 season.

events.name: Josh Daicos
events.note: Signed a six-year contract extension with Collingwood, alongside brother Nick Daicos, running through to the end of the 2030 season.

events.name: Sam Darcy
events.note: Re-signed with the Western Bulldogs on a two-year extension, keeping him at the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Sam Darcy
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, committing to the club until at least the end of 2029 ahead of impending free agency.

events.name: Luke Parker
events.note: Parker signed a five-year contract extension with Sydney, finalised around January 2016, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2021.

events.name: Luke Parker
events.note: Swans co-captain Parker rejected free agency and signed a four-year extension in 2021, committing to Sydney until the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Luke Parker
events.note: On Trade Period deadline day, Parker was traded from Sydney to North Melbourne (with Jacob Konstanty) in exchange for pick 44, ending his 14-year, 293-game Swans career; he signed a new deal with North Melbourne on arrival, exact length unconfirmed in available sources.

events.name: Jordon Sweet
events.note: Sweet, a rookie-listed ruckman yet to debut, re-signed with the Western Bulldogs for one further season, taking him through to at least the end of 2020.

events.name: Jordon Sweet
events.note: Still uncapped at AFL level, Sweet signed a further one-year rookie contract extension with the Bulldogs, with the club citing his development and a push to debut in 2021.

events.name: Jordon Sweet
events.note: After making his AFL debut in 2021, Sweet re-signed with the Western Bulldogs for a further two seasons, extending his contract to the end of 2023.

events.name: Jordon Sweet
events.reporter: AFL.com.au / Western Bulldogs FC / Port Adelaide FC
events.note: Sweet, out of contract and having requested a trade to his home state, was moved from the Western Bulldogs to Port Adelaide on the final day of the 2023 Trade Period in exchange for pick 50; he signed a three-year deal at Alberton through to the end of 2026, confirmed as his current deal per SEN's July 2026 report noting Port had begun re-signing talks.

events.name: Dylan Moore
events.note: Delisted by Hawthorn about a month after a strong final-round performance against Gold Coast, but the club had already committed to selecting him as a rookie, keeping his career alive.

events.name: Dylan Moore
events.note: Re-joined Hawthorn's list as a rookie selection (his 2020 season had been played mostly in scratch matches during COVID hub arrangements), becoming the 38th player signed to the Hawks' list for 2021.

events.name: Dylan Moore
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Hawthorn, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2023 season, after a breakout year kicking 27 goals in 20 games.

events.name: Dylan Moore
events.note: Turned down rival free-agency interest to sign a new three-year deal with Hawthorn, committing him to the club through the end of 2026.

events.name: Dylan Moore
events.note: Hawthorn vice-captain signed a four-year contract extension, locking him in through the end of 2030; he was already contracted through 2026 before this deal.

events.name: Sam Collins
events.note: Delisted by Fremantle at the conclusion of the 2017 season after 14 games across 2016-17; spent 2018 playing VFL for Werribee before being picked up by Gold Coast.

events.name: Sam Collins
events.note: Signed by Gold Coast as one of the club's mature-age state-league special assistance recruits (via Werribee VFL) ahead of the 2019 season, after being delisted by Fremantle.

events.name: Sam Collins
events.note: Extended his contract with the Suns for a further two years, through to the end of the 2022 season, around the time he was named to the club's leadership group.

events.name: Sam Collins
events.note: Suns vice-captain re-signed for a further three years, extending his contract from its 2022 expiry through to the end of 2025.

events.name: Sam Collins
events.note: Suns vice-captain and reigning club best-and-fairest signed a three-year contract extension to remain at Gold Coast until at least the end of 2028.

events.name: Harley Reid
events.note: Reid signed a two-year contract extension with West Coast, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2028 season, fending off strong interest from Victorian clubs (including St Kilda, Hawthorn and Essendon).

events.name: Ben Keays
events.note: Delisted by Brisbane along with Josh Walker and Ryan Bastinac after four seasons and 30 games; told he would not be offered a contract for 2020.

events.name: Ben Keays
events.note: Picked up by Adelaide with selection 7 in the 2019 AFL rookie draft after being delisted by Brisbane; exact draft-day date used as estimate.

events.name: Ben Keays
events.reporter: Adelaide FC (afc.com.au) - "Keays extends at West Lakes"
events.note: Signed a two-year extension in October 2021 to remain at Adelaide until the end of 2024; club GM Justin Reid praised his reliability and leadership qualities.

events.name: Ben Keays
events.reporter: Adelaide FC (afc.com.au) - "Ben Keays' journey from a Lion to Crows Vice Captain"
events.note: Signed a new three-year deal shortly after being appointed Crows vice-captain ahead of the 2024 season, keeping him at Adelaide through 2027.

events.name: Jake Bowey
events.note: Bowey signed a contract extension with Melbourne through the end of the 2028 season, announced by the club on 16 December 2025 following a 2025 season in which he averaged 22 disposals and finished fourth in Melbourne's best and fairest.

events.name: Liam Baker
events.note: Baker signed a two-year contract extension with Richmond, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2024 season.

events.name: Liam Baker
events.note: Baker was traded from Richmond to West Coast in a three-way deal also involving Carlton (which sent Matt Owies to West Coast), fulfilling his wish to return home to Western Australia. Trade date corroborated as October 15, 2024 (a Tuesday, matching the club article's timing); exact contract length signed with West Coast was not disclosed in available sources.

events.name: Mason Redman
events.note: Redman rejected free agency and a rival offer from Adelaide to sign a five-year extension with Essendon, becoming set to play his 100th game for the club.

events.name: Jack Macrae
events.note: Macrae signed a five-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, running through the end of the 2027 season, cementing him as a one-club player at the time.

events.name: Jack Macrae
events.note: Macrae was traded from Western Bulldogs to St Kilda (for pick 45, with Bulldogs receiving pick 17 and Matt Kennedy) as part of a four-club, three-player trade on the final day of the 2024 trade period, despite being contracted to the Bulldogs through 2027.

events.name: Jack Macrae
events.note: Upon being traded, Macrae signed a three-year contract with St Kilda as part of the 2024 Continental Tyres Trade Period, projected to run through the 2027 season.

events.name: Sam Berry
events.note: Berry signed a two-year contract extension with Adelaide, taking him through to the end of the 2026 season. Exact within-month announcement date is not stated on the source page, so late-August 2024 is used as an estimate based on surrounding news timing.

events.name: Lloyd Meek
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to Hawthorn along with a 2023 second-round pick, in exchange for Jaeger O'Meara moving to Fremantle. No contract length was disclosed.

events.name: Jack Ross
events.note: Richmond announced two-year contract extensions for Jack Ross, Josh Gibcus and Maurice Rioli Jr, taking Ross through to the end of 2024. Club GM Blair Hartley cited the trio's development.

events.name: Jack Ross
events.note: Jack Ross signed a further two-year contract extension with Richmond; end year inferred from the length of the deal since the source did not quote it directly.

events.name: Jack Ross
events.note: Jack Ross signed another two-year contract extension with Richmond, now contracted until the end of 2028. This is his current, active deal.

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield
events.note: Re-signed with Adelaide for three years following his breakout 2012 season, a deal well received by Crows supporters.

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield
events.note: Traded from Adelaide to Geelong after requesting a move to return to his Victorian hometown near Moggs Creek; deal completed in the October 2015 trade period.

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield
events.note: Signed a two-year extension as club captain alongside teammates Rhys Stanley and Mitch Duncan, tying him to Geelong through the end of 2026.

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield
events.note: Signed a one-year extension to play a 20th AFL season in 2027, putting the 400-game career milestone within reach.

events.name: Hugo Garcia
events.note: St Kilda confirmed a two-year contract extension for Hugo Garcia (drafted Pick 50, 2023 National Draft; debuted Round 5, 2024), keeping him at the club until the end of 2027. Announced alongside teammate Angus Hastie's extension; EGM of Football David Misson said the extra security would let both young players focus on their footy.

events.name: Wayne Milera
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension with Adelaide, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2020 (announced via the club's Facebook page on a Monday evening in April 2017; exact day not confirmed).

events.name: Wayne Milera
events.note: Signed a five-year contract extension with Adelaide, described as a 'monster' deal, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2025. He had been set to come out of contract at the end of the 2020 season.

events.name: Wayne Milera
events.note: Re-signed with Adelaide on a three-year extension, locking him in until the end of the 2028 season. Was previously out of contract at the end of 2025; the deal extends his tenure with the club to 13 years (also reported by Zero Hanger).

events.name: Jy Simpkin
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension (his first re-sign, three games into his debut season) taking him to the end of 2020. Article references 'last week's' Good Friday loss to the Western Bulldogs (14 Apr 2017), so exact publish date is estimated to late April 2017.

events.name: Jy Simpkin
events.note: Two-year extension announced 15 Aug 2019, keeping Simpkin at North Melbourne until the end of 2022; also reported by AFL.com.au as 'Two for Roo: Emerging mid inks new deal to end of 2022' (afl.com.au/news/129253).

events.name: Jy Simpkin
events.note: New deal signed 19 Oct 2021 (per embedded tweet timestamps), extending him to the end of 2024, shortly after his first Syd Barker Medal win; also covered by AFL.com.au (afl.com.au/news/685202).

events.name: Jy Simpkin
events.note: Five-year extension signed 26 May 2023 (as co-captain, dual Syd Barker medallist) taking him through to the end of 2029, on top of the season remaining on his prior deal. This remains his current, active contract; he was heavily linked with a trade to Collingwood in the 2025 trade period but North Melbourne rejected offers and he stayed at the club under this contract, losing the captaincy afterward. Also reported by AFL.com.au (afl.com.au/news/933099) and Zero Hanger (zerohanger.com/north-co-captain-jy-simpkin-signs-new-long-term-deal-137833).

events.name: Joel Jeffrey
events.note: Jeffrey signed a four-year contract extension with the Gold Coast Suns, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2028; announced 13 November 2023.

events.name: George Wardlaw
events.note: After an impressive debut, Wardlaw signed a two-year contract extension locking him in at North Melbourne until the end of 2026.

events.name: George Wardlaw
events.note: Wardlaw signed a further contract extension keeping him at North Melbourne until at least the end of 2028, after averaging 19 disposals and five tackles a game in 2026.

events.name: Josh Worrell
events.note: Worrell signed a two-year contract extension with Adelaide, recommitting to the club until at least the end of 2025.

events.name: Josh Worrell

events.name: Josh Worrell

events.name: Mac Andrew
events.note: Andrew, drafted at pick 5 in 2021, signed a two-year contract extension with Gold Coast before playing a senior game, taking him through to the end of 2025.

events.name: Mac Andrew
events.note: Andrew signed a five-year extension keeping him at Gold Coast through the end of 2030, with a games-based trigger clause that could extend the deal a further four years to 2034; he rejected interest from rival clubs including Hawthorn to re-sign.

events.name: Daniel Curtin
events.note: Curtin signed a three-year contract extension with Adelaide in June 2025, tying him to the Crows until at least the end of 2029.

events.name: Ryley Sanders
events.reporter: Western Bulldogs FC / National Indigenous Times
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Western Bulldogs until at least the end of the 2028 season, his first re-signing since being drafted with pick 6 in the 2023 National Draft.

events.name: Dan Houston
events.note: After completing a full season on Port Adelaide's senior list in 2018, Houston signed a three-year contract extension keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2022.

events.name: Dan Houston

events.name: Dan Houston
events.note: Houston was traded from Port Adelaide to Collingwood as part of a three-club, five-player mega trade (also involving Gold Coast), signing a six-year contract with the Magpies.

events.name: Karl Amon
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Port Adelaide, committing him through the 2018 and 2019 seasons.

events.name: Karl Amon
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension with Port Adelaide, securing his future until the end of the 2022 season.

events.name: Karl Amon
events.note: Left Port Adelaide as an unrestricted free agent and signed a four-year deal with Hawthorn; Port received pick No. 27 as compensation.

events.name: Karl Amon
events.note: Amon hit a games-based trigger in his Hawthorn contract activating a fifth season, tying him to the club through the end of 2027.

events.name: Nick Haynes

events.name: Nick Haynes
events.note: Haynes left GWS as an unrestricted free agent after 211 games and 13 seasons, signing a one-year deal with Carlton for the 2025 season with no compensation owed to GWS.

events.name: Nick Haynes

events.name: Ryan Lester

events.name: Ryan Lester

events.name: Ryan Lester

events.name: Ryan Lester
events.note: Lester signed a new one-year deal to remain at Brisbane through the 2026 season, his current active contract.

events.name: James Worpel

events.name: James Worpel

events.name: James Worpel

events.name: James Worpel

events.name: Bayley Fritsch

events.name: Bayley Fritsch

events.name: Harvey Thomas

events.note: Thomas signed a one-year contract extension, taking his deal through to the end of the 2026 season, after playing all 18 games and earning a Rising Star nomination in his debut year.

events.name: Harvey Thomas

events.name: Caleb Daniel
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Western Bulldogs through the end of the 2019 season.

events.name: Caleb Daniel
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, contracted through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Caleb Daniel
events.note: Traded from the Western Bulldogs to North Melbourne on the final day of the 2024 trade period, in exchange for a 2024 draft selection (pick 25). He moved to North Melbourne with two years still to run on his existing Bulldogs contract (through end of 2026).

events.name: Toby Bedford
events.note: Bedford requested a trade from Melbourne to GWS during the 2022 AFL trade period; GWS sent pick 44 to Melbourne to acquire him, and he signed a three-year deal with the Giants through the end of 2025.

events.name: Toby Bedford
events.reporter: Zero Hanger / GWS Giants official website / National Indigenous Times
events.note: Bedford signed a four-year contract extension with GWS, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2029 season.

events.name: Daniel Rioli

events.name: Daniel Rioli

events.name: Daniel Rioli

events.name: Daniel Rioli

events.name: Mark Blicavs

events.name: Mark Blicavs

events.name: Mark Blicavs

events.name: Connor Macdonald

events.name: Connor Macdonald

events.name: Massimo D'Ambrosio
events.note: D'Ambrosio requested a trade from Essendon and was moved to Hawthorn in the final minutes of the 2023 AFL Trade Period, with Essendon receiving pick No.61 and a future fourth-round selection; he signed a two-year contract with the Hawks.

events.name: Massimo D'Ambrosio

events.name: Jacob Hopper

events.name: Jacob Hopper

events.name: Sam Draper

events.name: Sam Draper
events.note: Draper signed a two-year extension keeping him at Essendon until at least the end of 2025, following a breakout 2022 season as first-choice ruckman.

events.name: Sam Draper
events.note: Draper left Essendon as an unrestricted free agent after nine seasons and signed with premiers Brisbane Lions; Essendon received an end-of-first-round compensation pick (pick 20) in the 2025 draft.

events.name: Tom McCartin

events.name: Tom McCartin

events.name: Tom McCartin

events.name: Lawson Humphries

events.name: Daniel Turner

events.name: Daniel Turner

events.name: Conor Nash

events.name: Conor Nash

events.name: Mitch McGovern

events.name: Mitch McGovern
events.note: McGovern was traded from Adelaide to Carlton in a three-way deal also involving Sydney, finalised 10 October 2018, after he requested a move despite having two years left on his Crows contract; he carried the remainder of that contract to Carlton.

events.name: Mitch McGovern

events.name: Mitch McGovern
events.note: After going undrafted-for-extension until the end of the trade period, McGovern signed a one-year contract extension with Carlton on reduced terms, keeping him at the club for 2026.

events.name: Reilly O'Brien
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Adelaide until at least the end of 2021, after taking over the club's number-one ruck role.

events.name: Reilly O'Brien

events.name: Reilly O'Brien

events.name: Charlie Cameron
events.note: Traded from Adelaide to Brisbane for pick 12 in the 2017 draft after requesting a move to be closer to family in Queensland; deal finalised in the final minutes of the trade period.

events.name: Charlie Cameron
events.note: Signed an early extension with Brisbane, adding four years to a deal that had been due to expire at the end of 2021, tying him to the club through the end of 2025.

events.name: Charlie Cameron
events.note: Signed a three-year extension on top of his existing deal (previously due to expire end of 2025), committing to Brisbane through the end of 2028 and saying he intends to finish his career there.

events.name: Colby McKercher
events.note: McKercher signed a two-year contract extension with North Melbourne, taking his deal through the end of the 2028 season (previously contracted to end of 2026). The deal keeps him off the market ahead of the Tasmania Devils' 2028 AFL entry.

events.name: Steele Sidebottom
events.note: Sidebottom, along with Luke Ball and Jarryd Blair, committed to a two-year contract extension with Collingwood, tying him to the club through the end of 2014.

events.name: Steele Sidebottom

events.name: Steele Sidebottom

events.name: Steele Sidebottom

events.name: Oliver Florent

events.note: Florent signed a two-year contract extension with Sydney, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2022.

events.note: Sydney traded Florent to Carlton for a future third-round draft pick on the final day of the 2025 AFL Trade Period.

events.name: Oliver Florent

events.name: Darcy Wilson
events.note: Wilson, who was out of contract at season's end and courted by rival clubs (including reported interest from North Melbourne with offers up to $1.2m/year), signed a two-year extension recommitting to St Kilda through the end of 2028.

events.name: Patrick Lipinski

events.name: Reuben Ginbey

events.note: Ginbey signed a three-year contract extension with West Coast, taking him through to the end of 2030 (his free agency year) and making him the longest-signed player at the club; he had already been contracted through 2027 before this extension.

events.name: Nick Vlastuin

events.name: Zac Williams

events.name: Tom Barrass
events.note: Signed a contract extension prior to the 2017 JLT Community Series, tying him to West Coast until the end of 2019. Included as last-resort Wikipedia sourcing after primary-source search budget was exhausted; could not independently verify with a club/AFL.com.au article.

events.name: Tom Barrass

events.name: Tom Barrass
events.note: Barrass spurned free agency to re-sign with West Coast for a further five years, tying him to the Eagles through 2027.

Media (including an Instagram post from a Hawthorn fan account) reported the accompanying deal as four years, but this could not be confirmed via an official club or AFL.com.au source within the available search budget, so length/end_year are left null rather than guessed.

events.name: Miles Bergman

events.name: Darcy Moore

events.note: Moore signed a six-year extension keeping him at Collingwood through the end of 2028, at the time as vice-captain (he became club captain in 2023).

events.name: Matthew Johnson
events.note: Johnson signed a four-year contract extension in May 2026, keeping him at Fremantle until at least the end of 2030.

events.name: Matt Roberts
events.note: Roberts signed a two-year contract extension with the Sydney Swans, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027; also confirmed by AFLRATINGS.

events.name: Logan Morris
events.note: Morris turned down rival interest from Collingwood and Melbourne to sign a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the Lions through the end of 2027.

events.name: Hayden Young
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension with Fremantle taking him through to the end of the 2027 season, on top of his existing deal through 2023.

events.name: Hayden Young
events.note: Signed a six-year extension on top of his existing deal (through 2027), taking him to 2033 and making him the AFL's longest-contracted player.

events.name: Kane Farrell
events.note: Farrell, along with Jase Burgoyne and Dylan Williams, signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Port Adelaide until the end of 2025.

events.name: Kane Farrell

events.name: Jack Higgins
events.note: Traded from Richmond to St Kilda during the 2020 trade period, with St Kilda sending picks in exchange; joined the Saints ahead of the 2021 season.

events.name: Jack Higgins
events.note: Re-signed with St Kilda on a four-year contract extension, locking him in at Moorabbin through the end of 2027.

events.name: Jack Higgins
events.note: Signed a further contract extension with St Kilda, taking him through to the end of 2029.

events.name: Darcy Jones
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with GWS, keeping him at the club until the end of 2026.

events.name: Darcy Jones
events.note: Signed a new two-year contract extension with GWS, locking him in until at least the end of the 2028 AFL season.

events.name: Jarrod Berry
events.note: Berry re-signed with Brisbane on a five-year deal through the end of 2029, turning down restricted free agency to stay with the club that drafted him.

events.name: Tom Powell
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with North Melbourne, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2024 (also confirmed by NMFC's own report the same day).

events.name: Tom Powell
events.note: Signed a further two-year contract extension keeping him at North Melbourne until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Tom Powell
events.note: Committed his future to North Melbourne with a new deal until at least the end of 2028, following a career-best 2025 season (published on the club site; exact announcement date within the 2025/26 off-season not specified in the source).

events.name: Luke Ryan
events.note: Ryan signed a three-year contract extension with Fremantle, adding to one year already remaining and keeping him at the club through the end of the 2023 season.

events.name: Luke Ryan
events.note: Ryan signed a four-year contract extension with Fremantle, on top of one year remaining on his prior deal, committing him to the Dockers until at least the end of 2027.

events.name: Sam De Koning
events.note: De Koning signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, tying him to the club until at least the end of the 2025 season (previous deal was due to expire end of 2023).

events.name: Sam De Koning
events.note: De Koning committed to Geelong on a fresh two-year contract extension, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027. This is his current, active deal.

events.name: Connor O'Sullivan
events.note: O'Sullivan signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2028; he had previously been contracted through the end of 2026.

events.name: Aaron Cadman
events.note: Cadman, already contracted for 2024, signed an early two-year contract extension with GWS taking him through to the end of 2026.

events.name: Aaron Cadman
events.note: Cadman signed a four-year contract extension with GWS, tying the No.1 draft pick to the club until the end of 2030, a day after kicking six goals against Geelong.

events.name: Rory Laird
events.note: After being elevated to Adelaide's senior list and earning a Rising Star nomination, Laird signed a two-year contract with the Crows in 2013.

events.name: Rory Laird
events.note: Off the back of a breakout 2015 season averaging 24.4 disposals, Laird signed a three-year contract extension with Adelaide, keeping him at the club through the end of 2018.

events.name: Rory Laird
events.note: Fresh off his first All-Australian selection, Laird signed a three-year contract extension to remain at Adelaide until at least the end of 2021.

events.name: Rory Laird
events.note: Facing unrestricted free agency at season's end, Laird committed his long-term future to Adelaide with a five-year contract extension running through the end of 2026.

events.name: Rory Laird
events.note: At age 32, Laird signed a one-year contract extension to remain at Adelaide through the end of 2027, extending his tenure into a 15th season with the club.

events.name: Ollie Wines
events.note: Wines, then vice-captain, re-signed with Port Adelaide on a four-year deal taking him through to the end of the 2022 season, forgoing free agency eligibility he would have had at the end of 2020.

events.name: Ollie Wines
events.note: With two years still to run on his prior deal, Wines signed a four-year extension locking him to Port Adelaide until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Dion Prestia
events.note: Re-signed with Gold Coast Suns on a three-year extension, taking him through to the end of 2016, after considering a move back to Victoria.

events.name: Dion Prestia
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Richmond (with pick 24, for pick 6 and a future second-round pick) after requesting a move home to Victoria; signed a five-year deal with the Tigers.

events.name: Dion Prestia
events.note: Signed a three-year extension with Richmond alongside Dylan Grimes, tying him to the club until the end of 2024.

events.name: Dion Prestia
events.note: Signed a one-year deal for the 2025 season, his ninth at Richmond, after finishing the 2024 season strongly.

events.name: Dion Prestia
events.note: Signed a one-year deal for the 2026 season, his 10th at Richmond and 16th in the AFL, after returning from an Achilles injury.

events.name: Jack Darling
events.reporter: Zero Hanger / AAP (syndicated via Canberra Times, Mandurah Mail, Western Advocate) / ESPN
events.note: Darling signed a five-year contract extension with West Coast, running through the 2024 season, fulfilling his stated wish to be 'an Eagle for life'.

events.name: Jack Darling
events.note: After requesting a trade to end his career closer to a premiership window, Darling was traded from West Coast to North Melbourne for a future 2024 fourth-round pick, signing on for what he described as a two-year stint at the Kangaroos.

events.name: Cooper Sharman
events.note: Sharman signed an extension tying him to St Kilda until the end of 2024, his first re-sign after his original 2-year rookie deal from late 2021.

events.name: Cooper Sharman
events.reporter: BigFooty News (citing St Kilda FC announcement)
events.note: Sharman signed a two-year contract extension alongside forward-line teammates Dan Butler and Lance Collard, keeping him at St Kilda beyond his 2024 expiry.

events.name: Cooper Sharman
events.note: Sharman signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at St Kilda until at least the end of 2028, following a career-best 2025 season (34 goals).

events.name: Lachie Schultz
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Fremantle at the end of 2021 (with an optional third year), keeping him at the club at least through the end of 2023 and turning down interest from Hawthorn.

events.name: Lachie Schultz
events.note: Playing his Round 13, 2023 match against Richmond automatically triggered a 12-month contract extension clause, securing Schultz at Fremantle through the end of 2024.

events.name: Lachie Schultz
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to Collingwood on day eight of the 2023 trade period after requesting the move to return to Victoria; Fremantle received pick 34 in the 2023 draft plus a future first-round selection.

events.name: Lachie Schultz
events.reporter: Collingwood FC (collingwoodfc.com.au); contract length per footyinfo.com player tracker
events.note: Signed with Collingwood as part of the trade from Fremantle; club-tracker sources list him as contracted through the end of 2027 (a multi-year deal), and this remains his active contract.

events.name: Taylor Walker
events.note: Walker signed a one-year contract extension to play a 15th AFL season in 2022, having been in career-best form (second in the Coleman Medal race).

events.name: Taylor Walker
events.note: Walker signed a one-year extension taking him into a 16th AFL season in 2023, saying 'I am going to be a Crow for life.'

events.name: Taylor Walker
events.note: Walker signed another one-year deal, extending into a 17th season at Adelaide (his 16th full AFL season), after passing 255 games and 590 career goals.

events.name: Taylor Walker
events.note: Walker officially extended his one-club career with a one-year deal to play an 18th AFL season in 2025.

events.name: Taylor Walker
events.note: Walker re-signed for a one-year deal to play a 19th AFL season in 2026, after booting 39 goals in 23 games in 2025 as Adelaide finished minor premiers.

events.name: Ned Long
events.note: Hawthorn delisted Long after five AFL games across the 2022-2023 seasons.

events.name: Ned Long
events.note: After being delisted by Hawthorn, Long joined Collingwood's VFL program and was elevated to the AFL list when the club selected him with Pick 19 in the 2024 Mid-Season Rookie Draft.

events.name: Ned Long
events.note: Long signed a one-year contract extension keeping him at Collingwood through the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Ned Long
events.note: Long signed a two-year contract extension, his first multi-year deal with Collingwood, running through the end of the 2027 season.

events.name: Joe Richards
events.note: Richards was traded from Collingwood to Port Adelaide in a three-club, five-player mega deal (also involving Gold Coast) completed on the second-last day of the 2024 AFL Trade Period, signing a three-year contract with the Power.

events.name: Brent Daniels
events.note: Daniels signed a four-year contract extension with GWS, committing him to the Giants until at least the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Brent Daniels
events.note: Coming off a career-best, All-Australian-squad season, Daniels signed a six-year contract extension keeping him at GWS until at least the end of 2031, taking him off the 2025 free agency market.

events.name: Peter Wright
events.note: Wright signed a one-year contract extension with Gold Coast, keeping him at the Suns through the end of 2017.

events.name: Peter Wright
events.note: Wright signed a further two-year extension with Gold Coast, keeping him at the club through the end of 2019, after a breakout 27-goal season.

events.name: Peter Wright
events.note: Wright re-committed to Gold Coast on a new deal extending his stay through the end of 2022; exact announcement date within 2019 not confirmed from the source.

events.name: Peter Wright
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Essendon for a future fourth-round draft selection; signed with the Bombers on a three-year deal through the end of 2023.

events.name: Peter Wright
events.note: Coming off a best-and-fairest 2022 season, Wright signed a four-year extension with Essendon keeping him at the club through the end of 2027.

events.name: Jack Graham
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Richmond, tying him to the club through the end of the 2020 season, shortly after his breakout 2017 Grand Final performance.

events.name: Jack Graham
events.note: Re-signed with Richmond on a new three-year deal through the end of 2023, rebuffing interest from Carlton and other rival clubs.

events.name: Jack Graham
events.note: Left Richmond as an unrestricted free agent to join West Coast on a four-year deal through 2028, with Richmond receiving a Band 4 compensation pick (pick 42) in the 2024 draft.

events.name: Jase Burgoyne
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Port Adelaide (alongside Kane Farrell and Dylan Williams), keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2025.

events.name: Jase Burgoyne

events.name: Brad Close
events.note: Signed a short-term contract extension alongside Lachie Henderson and Sam Simpson; the club did not disclose exact terms, but contemporaneous reporting described it as a one-year deal.

events.name: Brad Close
events.note: Close and Ollie Dempsey both signed two-year contract extensions, keeping Close at Geelong until at least the end of 2025.

events.name: Brad Close
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension on the eve of the 2025 season, committing to Geelong until at least the end of 2028; this is his current active deal.

events.name: Archie Roberts
events.note: Roberts, then in his first AFL season, signed a one-year contract extension with Essendon keeping him at the club through the end of 2026.

events.name: Archie Roberts
events.note: Following a breakout second season averaging 24 disposals from half-back, Roberts signed a further two-year extension, taking him from his existing deal through 2026 to the end of 2028.

events.name: Isaac Quaynor
events.note: Shortly after his senior debut in 2019, Collingwood added two years to Quaynor's standard rookie-tier contract, tying him to the club through the end of 2022.

events.name: Isaac Quaynor
events.note: Quaynor, then contracted for 2022, signed a three-year extension with Collingwood, securing his future to the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Isaac Quaynor
events.note: Off the back of Collingwood's 2023 premiership, Quaynor signed a five-year extension keeping him at the Magpies until at least the end of 2029.

events.name: Mason Wood
events.note: Delisted by North Melbourne at the end of the 2020 season as part of an 11-player list cull after seven seasons and 65 games at the Kangaroos.

events.name: Mason Wood
events.note: After a trial period, St Kilda added Wood to its rookie list via the pre-season supplemental selection period, giving him an AFL lifeline following his North Melbourne delisting.

events.name: Mason Wood
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension keeping him at St Kilda until at least the end of 2027, off the back of a breakout run as a wingman.

events.name: Xavier O'Halloran
events.note: O'Halloran agreed to a two-year contract extension with GWS, fending off interest from rival clubs after limited senior opportunities in his first two seasons.

events.name: Xavier O'Halloran
events.note: After a nervous wait through the trade period following a difficult 2022 season, O'Halloran secured a one-year contract extension to remain at GWS for 2023.

events.name: Xavier O'Halloran
events.note: O'Halloran signed a two-year contract extension with GWS, taking him into his seventh season at the club, after breaking out as a forward under new coach Adam Kingsley.

events.name: Xavier O'Halloran

events.name: Billy Frampton
events.note: Traded from Port Adelaide to Adelaide during the 2019 trade period, with Adelaide sending a future fourth-round pick (originally from GWS) to Port Adelaide in return.

events.name: Billy Frampton

events.name: Billy Frampton
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2028 season.

events.name: Will Hayward

events.name: Will Hayward

events.name: Will Hayward
events.note: Hayward was traded from Sydney to Carlton (with pick 11 and two future first-round picks) for Charlie Curnow, as part of a new contract adding a fifth year at his new club through to the end of 2030.

events.name: Jake Lloyd

events.note: Lloyd signed a four-year contract extension with Sydney, committing him to the Swans until at least the end of 2022.

events.name: Jake Lloyd

events.name: Jake Lloyd

events.name: Marcus Windhager
events.note: Windhager signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, tying him to the club through the end of the 2025 season, after a strong debut year.

events.name: Marcus Windhager

events.name: Adam Saad
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Essendon (Bombers gave up a future 2nd-round pick) and signed a three-year deal running through the end of 2020.

events.name: Adam Saad

events.name: Adam Saad

events.name: Errol Gulden

events.name: Errol Gulden
events.note: Gulden rejected a reported 10-year offer from a rival club and instead signed a four-year extension with Sydney, taking him through to the end of 2028 and to free agency.

events.name: Kai Lohmann
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane in the lead-up to the 2023 Preliminary Final (alongside teammate Darcy Wilmot), keeping him at the Lions through the end of 2025 after resisting interest from Victorian clubs.

events.name: Kai Lohmann
events.note: Signed a further two-year contract extension with Brisbane, announced weeks out from the start of the 2025 season, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2027.

events.name: Jye Caldwell
events.note: Traded from GWS Giants to Essendon on the final day of the 2020 trade period (Giants received pick 29 and a future 2nd-round pick for Caldwell, pick 44 and pick 74); he signed a reported five-year contract with the Bombers as part of the move.

events.name: Jye Caldwell
events.note: Re-signed with Essendon on a four-year contract extension, keeping him at the club through at least the end of the 2028 season, following a career-best 2024 campaign.

events.name: Daniel McStay
events.note: McStay signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the Lions until at least the end of 2017.

events.name: Daniel McStay

events.name: Daniel McStay
events.note: McStay left Brisbane as an unrestricted free agent after 9 seasons and signed a five-year deal with Collingwood early in the 2022 trade period; Brisbane received compensation pick 35. His contract currently runs through 2027 per Collingwood's official player listing.

events.name: Alex Pearce
events.note: Pearce, then 22, signed a two-year contract extension which, combined with one year remaining on his existing deal, kept him at Fremantle until at least the end of the 2020 season.

events.name: Alex Pearce
events.note: The 24-year-old defender, by then in Fremantle's leadership group, signed a further two-year extension taking him from his 2020 expiry through to the end of the 2022 season.

events.name: Alex Pearce

events.name: Alex Pearce
events.reporter: Fremantle FC / ESPN / National Indigenous Times
events.note: Fremantle captain Pearce, 29, signed a two-year extension through to the end of 2027, having been due to become a free agent at the end of 2025. This is his current, active deal.

events.name: Lachie Weller
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to Gold Coast during the 2017 trade period; Suns sent pick 2 and Brandon Matera to the Dockers to acquire Weller, who had requested a move home.

events.name: Lachie Weller
events.note: Signed a four-year deal with Gold Coast immediately upon completion of the trade from Fremantle.

events.name: Lachie Weller
events.note: Signed a new four-year contract extension, keeping him at Gold Coast through the end of 2026, shortly before returning from ACL rehabilitation.

events.name: Lachie Weller
events.note: Signed a long-term extension locking him in until the end of 2029, taking his Suns tenure beyond a decade, alongside teammate Bodhi Uwland's extension.

events.name: Jayden Short
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Richmond, keeping him at the club through the end of 2020.

events.name: Jayden Short
events.reporter: Footywire (Richmond FC), citing GM Blair Hartley
events.note: Re-signed with Richmond for a further two years, extending his deal through the end of 2022.

events.name: Jayden Short
events.note: Signed a five-year contract extension with Richmond, tying him to the club until the end of 2027; confirmed as his current deal by Zero Hanger's player profile ("Contracted Until: 2027").

events.name: Zach Guthrie
events.note: Guthrie signed a one-year extension with Geelong, part of a trio of contract announcements after the Cats' Round 1, 2024 win, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Zach Guthrie
events.note: Having already been committed to Geelong through the end of 2025, Guthrie signed a further three-year extension (alongside Jack Henry), taking his deal through to the end of the 2028 season.

events.name: Harry Morrison
events.note: Signed an extension with Hawthorn in June 2018 keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2020.

events.name: Harry Morrison
events.note: Committed to 'another year' with Hawthorn alongside Jack Scrimshaw and Oliver Hanrahan, reported alongside a review of his 2020 season.

events.name: Harry Morrison
events.note: Signed a two-year extension after a career-best 2022 season, keeping him at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2024.

events.name: Harry Morrison
events.note: Signed a two-year extension keeping him at Hawthorn until the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Harry Morrison
events.note: Signed a one-year extension keeping him at Hawthorn through the end of 2027, referencing his 130-game career; announced around mid-July 2026.

events.name: Isaac Cumming
events.note: Cumming left GWS as an unrestricted free agent and signed with Adelaide; the Crows paid no trade compensation, with GWS instead receiving Adelaide's future first-round pick (then pick 21) as free agency compensation.

events.name: Bailey J. Williams
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at West Coast through the end of the 2022 season, his first re-signing after being drafted with pick 35 in 2018.

events.name: Bailey J. Williams
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension alongside Nic Naitanui, tying him to West Coast through the end of the 2024 season.

events.name: Bailey J. Williams
events.note: Rejected restricted free agency to sign a six-year contract extension with West Coast, running through the end of the 2032 season, after a breakout 2026 season.

events.name: Jordan De Goey
events.reporter: Anthony Colangelo & Michael Gleeson, The Age
events.note: De Goey re-signed with Collingwood for two years, turning down multi-year, multi-million dollar offers from North Melbourne and St Kilda.

events.name: Jordan De Goey
events.note: De Goey signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood, confirmed in December 2020.

events.name: Jordan De Goey
events.note: After Collingwood withdrew a contract offer in June 2022 following a Bali nightclub incident, and a lengthy standoff over behavioural clauses, De Goey signed a five-year extension (with behavioural conditions applying to the first two years) to remain at Collingwood until at least the end of 2027, rejecting interest from St Kilda.

events.name: Alex Neal-Bullen
events.note: After a strong debut season, Melbourne added an extra year to Neal-Bullen's contract (he was already contracted for 2016), taking him through to the end of 2017.

events.name: Alex Neal-Bullen
events.note: Signed a two-year extension with Melbourne, locking him in through the end of the 2019 season; GM of Football Operations Josh Mahoney cited his progress through 2017. Exact month/day of announcement not stated in the article, so date is estimated to mid-2017.

events.name: Alex Neal-Bullen
events.note: After an uncertain 2020 trade period, Neal-Bullen signed a two-year extension roughly 10 rounds into the 2021 season, taking him through to the end of 2023. Article gives no exact date, so mid-May 2021 (approx. round 10) is used as an estimate.

events.name: Alex Neal-Bullen
events.note: Having qualified for free agency in 2023, Neal-Bullen re-signed with Melbourne on a three-year deal through to the end of 2026 (Melbourne FC: 'Neal-Bullen signs three-year deal', https://www.melbournefc.com.au/news/1317507/neal-bullen-signs-three-year-deal). Superseded by his October 2024 trade to Adelaide before it could run its course.

events.name: Alex Neal-Bullen
events.note: Traded from Melbourne to Adelaide on day one of the 2024 trade period (Adelaide sent pick 28 to Melbourne) after requesting a move home to South Australia for family reasons; signed a four-year deal with the Crows through to the end of 2028. Terms corroborated by SEN (https://www.sen.com.au/news/2024/10/08/thats-not-a-fair-trade-cornes-issue-with-melbournes-alex-neal-bullen-deal). This is his current, active contract.

events.name: Cam Mackenzie
events.note: Six months after Hawthorn drafted him with pick 7 in the 2022 AFL Draft, the 19-year-old signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Hawthorn through the end of 2026.

events.name: Cam Mackenzie
events.note: Amid a career-best 2026 season, Mackenzie signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2028.

events.name: Jacob van Rooyen
events.note: As a 19-year-old yet to debut at AFL level, van Rooyen signed a contract extension with Melbourne keeping him at the club through the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Jacob van Rooyen
events.note: Having been due to hit free agency at the end of 2025, van Rooyen turned down interest from WA clubs and signed a four-year contract extension with Melbourne, tying him to the club until the end of 2029.

events.name: Mitch Owens
events.note: Owens signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, keeping him at the club through the end of 2025.

events.name: Mitch Owens
events.note: Owens signed a four-year contract extension, re-signing with St Kilda until the end of the 2029 season.

events.name: Finn O'Sullivan
events.note: O'Sullivan signed a two-year contract extension with North Melbourne, keeping him at Arden Street through the end of 2029, having knocked back a rival approach from expansion club Tasmania.

events.name: Tom McCarthy
events.reporter: West Coast Eagles official website / AFL (Nathan Schmook)
events.note: After a standout debut half-season (23.6 disposals per game across 10 games following his selection with pick 1 in the 2025 mid-season rookie draft), McCarthy signed a two-year contract extension with West Coast, keeping him at the club through the end of 2028.

events.name: Liam Ryan
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension tying him to West Coast until at least the end of 2022.

events.name: Liam Ryan
events.reporter: West Coast Eagles official website / National Indigenous Times
events.note: Signed a two-year extension (on top of his existing 2024 contract) committing him to West Coast until the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Liam Ryan
events.note: Traded from West Coast to St Kilda (Saints sent their 2026 second-round pick to West Coast, plus a future 2027 third-round pick) after Ryan, still contracted for 2026, requested a move; reported to have signed a four-year deal with St Kilda.

events.name: James O'Donnell
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, keeping him at the club through the end of 2025, after an impressive start to his rookie season.

events.name: James O'Donnell
events.reporter: AFL.com.au / Western Bulldogs FC / Zero Hanger
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, keeping him at the club until the end of 2027, well ahead of his prior deal's October 2025 expiry.

events.name: James Jordon
events.note: Delisted by Melbourne at the end of the 2020 season as part of a list-management move.

events.name: James Jordon
events.note: Immediately re-signed by Melbourne as a rookie-listed player after being delisted; this rookie re-signing was what later made him eligible for unrestricted free agency after the 2023 season.

events.name: James Jordon

events.name: Jaxon Prior

events.name: Judd McVee

Exact signing date not separately confirmed from the trade date, so estimated as coinciding with the October 8, 2025 trade.

events.name: Tyson Stengle

events.name: Tyson Stengle
