events.name: Ned Reeves
events.note: Turned back interest from a rival club (reported to be Carlton) to re-sign with Hawthorn on a three-year extension, taking him to the end of 2029. Corroborated by Zero Hanger, Hawk Talk Podcast/AFL on X, and mirrored on Hawthorn FC's own site under 'Reeves recommits' (same event). This is his current active contract.

events.name: Liam Stocker
events.note: As a 19-year-old, Stocker agreed to a two-year contract extension with Carlton, keeping him at the club "until at least the end of 2022".

events.name: Liam Stocker
events.note: Delisted by Carlton after playing 6 matches in 2022 (28 games total across 2019-2022); corroborated by AFL.com.au ("First-round pick Liam Stocker among delisted Carlton Blues") and SEN.

events.name: Liam Stocker
events.note: Signed by St Kilda as a rookie via the pre-season Supplemental Selection Period (SSP) ahead of the 2023 season, months after being delisted by Carlton. Announcement date used; St Kilda had until 15 Feb 2023 to finalise SSP signings.

events.name: Liam Stocker
events.note: One-year extension into 2024, announced alongside Jimmy Webster, Ryan Byrnes and Zak Jones. Article states the 2023 Trade Period "commenced today" (2 Oct 2023), used to estimate the publish date since no explicit date was visible on the page.

events.name: Liam Stocker
events.note: One-year extension through the 2025 season, one of six Saints re-signed together (also Jimmy Webster, Ryan Byrnes, Angus McLennan, Max Heath, Isaac Keeler). Mirrored by saints.com.au "Six Saints sign on" (news/1647426).

events.name: Liam Stocker
events.note: One-year extension keeping Stocker at St Kilda "until the end of 2026", part of a group of five re-signings (also Dougal Howard, Isaac Keeler, Paddy Dow, Liam O'Connell). Mirrored by saints.com.au "Saints lock in five for 2026" (news/1868972). This is his current, active contract; Zero Hanger's player-profile page separately lists him as "Contracted Until 2026".

events.name: Jacob Konstanty
events.reporter: North Melbourne FC / Sydney Swans FC
events.note: Traded from Sydney to North Melbourne along with Luke Parker in exchange for pick 44 in the 2024 AFL draft, at the close of the 2024 Trade Period. Exact date corroborated via Wikipedia and a BigFooty thread opened that day.

events.name: Jacob Konstanty
events.note: Signed with North Melbourne as part of the trade that brought him from Sydney; length of this initial NM contract was not publicly disclosed in club reporting.

events.name: Jacob Konstanty
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at North Melbourne until at least the end of the 2028 season (per club head of football talent Brady Rawlings). Exact day/month of signing not published; corroborated by Zero Hanger listing him as 'Contracted until 2028'.

events.name: Cooper Hynes
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, taking him through to the end of 2029. Club quote from Sam Power (EM of Men's Football) cited his move to the wing and a recent Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Hunter Clark
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at St Kilda through the end of 2025, following his return from injury to play 19 games in 2023's finals campaign. Also reported by St Kilda FC official site (saints.com.au/news/1450409/clark-puts-pen-to-paper-on-fresh-extension).

events.name: Hunter Clark
events.note: Signed a further two-year extension (alongside teammate Jack Higgins) locking him in at St Kilda through the end of 2027; confirmed by St Kilda Insider (Instagram) as 're-signed with St Kilda until the end of 2027 on a 2-year extension'. This is his current active contract as of August 2026 - no newer extension found despite a hard multi-angle search (Wikipedia, AFL.com.au, Zero Hanger site search, DuckDuckGo/Google/Bing searches for 2026/2028/2029/2030 terms).

events.name: Leek Aleer
events.note: Two-year contract extension keeping Aleer at GWS through to 2027, signed days after St Kilda withdrew from a trade for the 24-year-old defender following his September 2025 trade request. Corroborated by Fox Footy (https://www.foxsports.com.au/afl/afl-trade-deadline-2025-leek-aleer-signs-new-contract-with-gws-giants-after-st-kilda-backflip/news-story/63e0de32bf59c3b00a1259e3486e3347).

events.name: Bailey Banfield
events.note: Signed a new two-year contract with Fremantle keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2020, alongside his promotion from the rookie list to the senior list following a strong debut 2018 season. Corroborated by an afl.com.au article of the same date: http://www.afl.com.au/news/2018-08-15/new-deal-promotion-for-dockers-rookie

events.name: Bailey Banfield
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Fremantle keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026, after entering 2024 as an unrestricted free agent and reportedly attracting interest from Victorian clubs. Article publish date (6 September 2024) used as event date since exact signing date wasn't stated; direct fetch of thewest.com.au was blocked during research, so this is sourced via the citation/summary on Bailey Banfield's Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailey_Banfield). This is his current contract.

events.name: Toby Pink
events.note: Signed by North Melbourne as a delisted free agent, four years after being delisted by Sydney at the end of 2019 (having never played a senior game for the Swans). Also corroborated by AFLRATINGS (13 Oct 2023, 'Toby Pink joins Nth Melbourne', https://aflratings.com.au/2023/10/13/toby-pink-joins-nth-melbourne/) and by AFL.com.au's 14 Mar 2024 debut preview article.

events.name: Toby Pink
events.note: North Melbourne article 'Roos trio sign on for 2025': after playing 15 senior games in 2024, Pink triggered a one-year contract extension through the end of 2025 (alongside Will Phillips and Robert Hansen Jr., also one-year deals through 2025). Exact publication date not shown on the page/could not be recovered from Wayback Machine (blocked); date estimated to mid-October 2024, around the end of the 2024 trade period, based on the article's framing of the trigger following the completed 2024 season.

events.name: Jacob Wehr
events.note: Signed with Port Adelaide as an unrestricted free agent (nil compensation to GWS) during the 2025 free agency period, joining for the 2026 season after five seasons at GWS Giants (drafted pick 59, 2020 draft; 39 games 2022-2025). Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps: 'At 27-years-old, he will provide experience and depth to our talented midfield group.' Contract length/end year not disclosed in available sources.

events.name: Harry Rowston
events.note: Two-year contract extension signed just after his AFL debut (round 2, 2023), tying him to GWS until at least the end of 2026. He was already contracted for 2023 as a GIANTS Academy graduate taken with pick 16 in the 2022 AFL Draft.

events.name: Harry Rowston
events.note: New two-year contract extension, keeping Rowston at GWS until at least the end of the 2028 AFL season; he was already contracted for 2026 at the time. Announced ahead of the 2025 Kevin Sheedy Medal, following a breakout round-17 performance (4 goals) that earned an AFL Rising Star nomination.

events.name: James Borlase
events.note: Delisted by Adelaide after playing 4 AFL games in 2023, but the club publicly committed to redrafting him as a rookie for 2024 (rookie 'lifeline').

events.name: James Borlase
events.note: Re-signed by Adelaide on a two-year contract extension through the end of 2026, following a breakout 10-game 2024 season. Also reported by the club at https://www.afc.com.au/news/1653201/four-young-crows-sign-on. This is his current active deal.

events.name: Tyler Brockman
events.note: Out of contract at Hawthorn after the 2023 season, Brockman requested a trade home to WA (reported by Callum Twomey, AFL.com.au, 30 Aug 2023: https://www.afl.com.au/news/1020648/hawthorn-hawks-small-forward-tyler-brockman-seeks-trade-back-to-wa). He was traded to West Coast on 14 October 2023, per Wikipedia citing an AFL House confirmation tweet. No extension/re-signing has been reported since. Zero Hanger's live off-contract-2026 list (fetched 2026-08-10, https://www.zerohanger.com/afl/players/off-contract-2026/) still lists Brockman among West Coast's off-contract players, confirming this WCE deal runs through the end of the 2026 season and is his current contract; he does not appear on Zero Hanger's 2027 off-contract list.

events.name: Mykelti Lefau
events.note: Signed a rookie-list contract with Richmond after being invited to trial during the pre-season Supplemental Selection Period (SSP) ahead of the 2024 season; made his AFL debut just 34 days later in Round 2, 2024. Date is back-calculated from the article's '34 days before his March 24, 2024 debut' and is therefore estimated — no exact signing date is stated. No contract length/value disclosed. No re-signing or extension has been reported since; this remains his current, active deal (confirmed still absent from 2026 off-contract/free-agency lists).

events.name: Jack Williams
events.note: One-year extension announced alongside Jeremy McGovern, Jamie Cripps and Jack Petruccelle, tying Williams to West Coast until the end of 2024. He was 19, drafted with pick 57 in 2021, and had played 9 senior matches (8 that season) at the time of signing.

events.name: Jack Williams
events.note: Two-year extension signed midway through his third season on West Coast's list (21 games played), tying him to the Eagles through the end of 2026. West Coast GM of Football Gavin Bell praised him as 'a key forward who can also pinch-hit in the ruck.' No newer (2025/2026) re-signing was found in AFLRATINGS, Zero Hanger, or West Coast's own news feed as of this research, so this remains his active deal.

events.name: Matthew Cottrell
events.note: Signed a new two-year contract extension, contracted through the end of 2024, alongside clubmates Matthew Owies, Sam Durdin and Josh Honey; announced by Carlton Head of List Management Nick Austin.

events.name: Matthew Cottrell
events.note: Signed a new three-year contract extension, now contracted through the end of 2027; current deal as of Aug 2026 (no subsequent re-sign, trade, delisting or retirement found despite missing most of 2024 with a fractured shoulder and starting 2026 on the sidelines after knee surgery).

events.name: Dante Visentini
events.note: Two-year contract extension announced 21 Feb 2025, keeping Visentini at Port Adelaide through the end of 2027; he was entering his fourth season at the club at the time. No prior re-signing found (his original entry was via the 2021 national draft, pick 56), so this is his first extension and is his current active deal as of Aug 2026.

events.name: Bo Allan
events.note: Original/initial listing contract: Bo Allan selected by West Coast Eagles with pick 16 (round 1) in the 2024 AFL National Draft (20-21 Nov 2024), recruited from Peel Thunder (WAFL). Extensive multi-angle search (Wikipedia player page + citations, 2024 draft page, AFL.com.au, West Coast Eagles official site, FootyWire, multiple search engines, local ListTrac contract archives) found no evidence of any subsequent re-signing/extension - he remains a very recent draftee still on his first contract as of this research (Aug 2026), so this draft signing is returned as the anchor event per instructions. Exact contract length not confirmed by any source and left null rather than assumed.

events.name: Xavier Lindsay
events.note: Selected by Melbourne with pick 11 in the 2024 AFL national draft (from Gippsland Power/Coates Talent League); no re-signing or extension has since been reported. This is his original/first AFL contract, still current — Zero Hanger's player profile lists him as contracted to Melbourne through 2027.

events.name: Maurice Rioli
events.note: Richmond announced simultaneous two-year contract extensions for Jack Ross, Josh Gibcus and Maurice Rioli Jr, taking Rioli through to the end of 2024. GM of Football Talent Blair Hartley cited the trio's development.

events.name: Maurice Rioli
events.note: Signed a further two-year extension with Richmond through to the end of 2026. Blair Hartley: 'Maurice has worked hard on his game across his four years with us and should take great confidence into next year from the form he was able to produce when fit and firing.' No newer extension could be confirmed despite an extensive search covering AFLRATINGS' full post archive, Google News, Richmond FC and AFL.com.au, so this remains his current active deal.

events.name: Laitham Vandermeer
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, locking him in at the Western Bulldogs until the end of 2023 (from pick 37, 2018 draft).

events.name: Laitham Vandermeer

events.name: Laitham Vandermeer
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension, keeping him at the Western Bulldogs until at least the end of 2028 (his current/active deal).

events.name: Nick Holman
events.note: Selected by Gold Coast with pick 19 (round 2) in the 2018 rookie draft (held 27 Nov 2017), following two SANFL seasons at Central District after being delisted by Carlton. This is his entry contract at Gold Coast, included as the club-arrival anchor event since he later re-signed multiple times at the Suns.

events.name: Nick Holman

events.name: Nick Holman
events.note: "Nick Holman has signed a one-year contract extension (via Gold Coast)." Most recent confirmed re-signing found; he remains an active Gold Coast player through round 20 of the 2026 season (144 games, per Wikipedia/club coverage), so this is marked as his current deal even though a later 2025/2026 extension may exist that a hard search could not surface — no dated article for any subsequent re-signing was found despite extensive searching (AFLRATINGS post archives, club site, Wikipedia, search engines).

events.name: Sam Powell-Pepper
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension on top of his original mandated two-year draft contract (pick 18, 2016), keeping him at Port Adelaide until the end of 2020.

events.note: Agreed to terms on a three-year contract extension, keeping him at Port Adelaide until the end of 2023.

events.name: Sam Powell-Pepper
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, keeping him at Port Adelaide until the end of 2025.

events.name: Sam Powell-Pepper
events.note: Signed a four-year extension with one year still to run on his prior deal, taking him through until at least the end of 2029. This is his current active contract; he has been sidelined by ACL injuries in 2024-2026 but remains contracted to Port Adelaide.

events.name: Oscar Allen
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension tying him to West Coast until at least the end of 2025; club statement noted he was 'already contracted to the end of 2022' before this deal, i.e. this is a re-signing, not his original draft contract (pick 21, 2017 draft).

events.name: Oscar Allen
events.note: Left West Coast (where he had been co-captain) as a restricted free agent when West Coast chose not to match Brisbane's offer; West Coast received pick 2 as compensation. Also confirmed by Brisbane's own announcement ('Allen becomes a Lion', https://www.lions.com.au/news/1912099/allen-becomes-a-lion) and by AFLRATINGS (https://aflratings.com.au/2025/10/08/oscar-allen-joins-brisbane/). Contract length/end year were not publicly disclosed in any of these reports (West Coast had confirmed on 24 Aug 2025 that Allen intended to test restricted free agency: https://www.westcoasteagles.com.au/news/1874374/club-statement-oscar-allen). This is his current, active contract as of mid-2026.

events.name: Steven May
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Melbourne (with Kade Kolodjashnij) for pick No.6 and No.23, as part of the Jesse Hogan/Fremantle trade chain, during the 2018 AFL trade period.

events.name: Steven May
events.note: Joined Melbourne on a five-year deal upon arriving via trade from Gold Coast; article states he 'joins the club on a five-year deal' without quoting an explicit end year, so 2023 is inferred (2019 start + 5 years).

events.name: Steven May
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, explicitly keeping him at Melbourne 'until the end of 2025' ('An incredible asset': Demons secure May on new deal).

events.name: Steven May
events.note: Quietly signed a one-year extension during the 2024 season (exact signing date never publicised) adding a year to his deal, locking him in 'until the end of 2026' — only revealed publicly by AFL.com.au's Inside Trading column in March 2025 ('Steven May is locked in until the end of 2026 after quietly penning an extension last year').

events.name: Steven May
events.note: Announced retirement via Instagram on the eve of the 2026 season; the headline itself notes he called time 'despite one year remaining on deal', confirming his 2024 extension ran through the end of 2026.

events.name: Harry Dean
events.note: Harry Dean's original/initial contract: selected by Carlton with father-son Pick No.3 in the 2025 AFL Draft (matching a West Coast bid), officially signing with the club. Player profile lists him as contracted until 2028 (Zero Hanger: https://www.zerohanger.com/afl/players/harry-dean/). He has not re-signed since — this is his only and current contract, included as the anchor event per instructions since no re-signing has occurred.

events.name: Arthur Jones
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Western Bulldogs through the end of 2025, after breaking into the senior side in round 3, 2023 (corroborated by Zero Hanger, published 19 Apr 2023).

events.name: Arthur Jones
events.note: Signed a one-year extension (alongside Josh Dolan and Michael Sellwood) adding 12 months to his deal, keeping him at the Western Bulldogs until at least the end of 2026. This is his current active contract.

events.name: Jack Payne
events.note: Signed a 5-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2029. He was already contracted for 2024 prior to this deal. Announced Aug 2, 2023; also reported by ESPN (https://www.espn.com/afl/story/_/id/38119732/afl-brisbane-lions-defender-jack-payne-signs-another-five-years) and confirmed as his current deal by Zero Hanger's player profile (Contracted Until 2029).

events.name: Riley Hardeman
events.note: One-year contract extension announced 4 Sep 2024 (per Tom Morris/9News, corroborated by AFLRATINGS), keeping Hardeman at North Melbourne until at least the end of 2026, alongside clubmate Wil Dawson. This is his current active deal: as of Aug 2026 he is out of contract at season's end and has not yet signed the reported 2-year offer (AFL.com.au 'Inside Trading', ~Aug 2026) that would extend him to 2028.

events.name: Corey Warner
events.note: As an 18-year-old developing on the Swans' VFL list, Warner extended his contract alongside brother Chad Warner, staying at Sydney until at least the end of 2025.

events.name: Corey Warner
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Sydney until at least the end of 2027, following strong VFL form; confirmed as his current deal on Zero Hanger's player profile ('Contracted Until 2027') as of the 2026 season.

events.name: Hamish Davis
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension, adding a year onto his original two-year draftee deal (from being drafted with pick 65 in the 2024 AFL Draft), taking him through to the end of 2027. Announced alongside fellow young Eagles Lucca Grego and Tom Gross in the article 'Young trio recommit at Eagles'. Multiple secondary sources (BigFooty Contracts Thread, web search metadata) place the announcement in June 2025, but the exact day is not confirmed on the primary source page (no visible byline/date), hence date is estimated to mid-month. Corroborated by FootyWire player page, which lists him as 'out of contract at the end of 2027'. Original mandatory draft contract skipped per instructions since he has since re-signed.

events.name: Oskar Baker
events.note: Delisted by Melbourne after five seasons and 15 AFL games, ending his tenure at the club.

events.name: Oskar Baker
events.note: Signed by Western Bulldogs as a delisted free agent via the pre-season supplemental selection period, joining as a rookie for 2023.

events.name: Oskar Baker
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, tying him to the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Oskar Baker
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension (alongside Nick Coffield), keeping him at the Western Bulldogs through the 2026 season. This is his current active contract.

events.name: James Harmes
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Melbourne, locking him in until at least the end of 2020.

events.name: James Harmes
events.note: Signed a new long-term deal with Melbourne (already contracted for 2020, deal added four more years), extending him to the end of 2024. Exact day-of-month not stated; October 2019 per contemporaneous reporting.

events.name: James Harmes
events.note: Traded from Melbourne to the Western Bulldogs for a future third-round draft pick, after requesting a move at the end of the 2023 season.

events.name: James Harmes
events.note: Signed a three-year contract with the Western Bulldogs upon arrival via trade from Melbourne, running through the end of 2026.

events.name: James Harmes
events.note: Announced immediate retirement after 174 games and 12 AFL seasons (Melbourne 2014-2023, Western Bulldogs 2024-2025), with one season still remaining on his three-year Western Bulldogs contract.

events.name: Jack Hutchinson
events.reporter: West Coast Eagles official site / AFL.com.au
events.note: Announced Fri 23 May 2025 alongside Tim Kelly and Tyrell Dewar. Hutchinson (arrived via 2024 Mid-Season Draft from Collingwood's VFL side, pick 3) was already contracted for 2026; signed a further three-year extension on top of that, taking him to the end of 2029. Quote: "I'm super pumped, coming over less than a year ago and to now re-sign is amazing." Corroborated by AFL.com.au (https://www.afl.com.au/news/1327072/pumped-key-midfielder-tim-kelly-among-west-coast-eagles-trio-put-pen-to-paper-on-new-deals) and Zero Hanger (https://www.zerohanger.com/west-coast-midfielder-among-three-to-earn-extensions-162823/). His original mandatory contract from the 2024 Mid-Season Draft (pick 3, West Coast, 29 May 2024) is superseded by this extension and is omitted per instructions.

events.name: Christian Moraes
events.note: Extended his existing contract (which ran to end of 2026) by a further 12 months, keeping him at Port Adelaide until at least the end of 2027. Announced alongside teammates Jack Whitlock and Tom Cochrane. Original mandatory contract from his 2024 draft (pick 38) is superseded/skipped per instructions since he has since re-signed.

events.name: Hugh Boxshall
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda (announced alongside teammate Max Hall), taking him through to the end of 2028. This built on his original deal signed after being drafted with pick 45 in the 2024 AFL Draft (a 2-year deal covering 2025-2026), which is not listed separately since he has since re-signed.

events.name: Jack Lukosius
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension with Gold Coast, committing until the end of 2026 (originally drafted pick 2, 2018 draft). Also reported by Gold Coast FC (https://www.goldcoastfc.com.au/news/1154953/jack-lukosius-locked-in-until-2026) and AFLRATINGS (https://aflratings.com.au/2022/06/23/contract-update-jack-lukosius/).

events.name: Jack Lukosius
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Port Adelaide as part of a three-club deal (with Collingwood) on the second-last day of the 2024 AFL Trade Period, despite having two years remaining on his Gold Coast contract. Port Adelaide sent Dan Houston (among other assets) to Gold Coast/Collingwood; Port received Lukosius, Joe Richards, Rory Atkins and draft picks.

events.name: Jack Lukosius
events.note: Signed a new six-year contract with Port Adelaide as part of landing at the club via the three-team trade, running through the end of the 2030 season. Six-year length also corroborated by AFL journalist Tom Morris (https://twitter.com/tommorris32/status/1838365154070925653). This is Lukosius's current active deal.

events.name: Luke Cleary
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Western Bulldogs until at least the end of 2025; at the time he was a 21-year-old developing defender who had played four senior games since being taken at Pick 61 in the 2021 draft. Corroborated by the club's own article 'Cleary locked away until 2025' (https://www.westernbulldogs.com.au/news/1300440/cleary-locked-away-until-2025).

events.name: Luke Cleary
events.note: Signed a further two-year extension (alongside teammate Lachlan Smith) taking him to the end of the 2027 season, announced as Cleary, 23, was playing reliable senior football as a defender. Corroborated by the club's own article 'Cleary & Smith commit to the Kennel' (https://www.westernbulldogs.com.au/news/1794386/cleary-smith-commit-to-the-kennel). This is his current active contract.

events.name: Brandon Zerk-Thatcher
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Essendon through at least the end of 2021; article states he was 20 years old and had not yet made his senior debut (which came Round 22, 2019), so month is estimated as mid-2019.

events.name: Brandon Zerk-Thatcher
events.note: Signed a further two-year extension, committing to Essendon through 2023; article describes him as 22 years old (born Aug 1998) with 17 career appearances, so exact month is estimated. Essendon reportedly later tabled a three-year offer to keep him beyond 2023 (per AFL.com.au, 'Dons defender rejects three-year deal, requests interstate move'), which he declined before requesting a trade home to South Australia.

events.name: Brandon Zerk-Thatcher
events.note: Traded from Essendon to Port Adelaide (with pick 73 and two future fourth-round picks) in exchange for Xavier Duursma, finalised on the last day of the 2023 Continental Tyres AFL Trade Period. He had been out of contract at Essendon after rejecting a three-year offer and requested the move to return to his home state of South Australia.

events.name: Brandon Zerk-Thatcher
events.note: New contract signed with Port Adelaide as part of the trade from Essendon (arrived ahead of the 2024 season). Zero Hanger's player profile lists him as 'Contracted Until: 2026'; a Zero Hanger roundup published 5 Aug 2026 ('Delist, keep or trade: Port Adelaide's out-of-contract 22', https://www.zerohanger.com/delist-keep-or-trade-port-adelaides-out-of-contract-22-180795/) confirms he is out of contract at season's end and among the club's out-of-contract players for 2027. Exact signing date and contract length in years were not found in a primary club announcement; date is estimated as the trade date.

events.name: Mitchell Edwards
events.note: Signed a contract extension (alongside Shaun Mannagh) keeping him at Geelong 'until at least the end of 2028'. Article published 2025-04-10. Edwards was originally drafted with Pick 32 in the 2023 AFL Draft; this extension is used as the anchor event for his contract timeline since he later re-signed again.

events.name: Mitchell Edwards
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension to remain at Geelong 'until at least the end of 2030', announced shortly after his Round 21 2026 AFL Rising Star nomination (per Wikipedia, 'In July 2026'). Exact day within July 2026 not confirmed on the club article, so date is estimated to the 15th. This is his current active deal.

events.name: Billy Wilson
events.note: One-year contract extension signed with Carlton, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026. Announced after his AFL debut (Round 16, 2025) and strong form at VFL/AFL level; List Manager Nick Austin praised his 'flair and dash off the half-back line'. Exact day-of-month for the announcement could not be independently confirmed from the article page itself (no visible byline date), so flagged as estimated.

events.name: Billy Wilson
events.note: Two-year contract extension signed with Carlton, keeping him at IKON Park until at least the end of 2028. Announced mid-2026 season after a run of 8 consecutive AFL games off half-back (4 games with 22+ disposals); GM of Football Chris Davies cited his composure and reading of the game. Confirmed as his current deal by Zero Hanger player profile ('Contracted Until 2028'). Exact day-of-month for the announcement could not be independently confirmed from the article page itself (no visible byline date), so flagged as estimated.

events.name: Elijah Hollands
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Carlton on the final day of the 2023 trade period, in exchange for a future 3rd-round selection (via Essendon) and a future 4th-round selection, with a minor pick swap (Carlton's pick 26 for Gold Coast's pick 28).

events.name: Elijah Hollands
events.note: Signed his contract with Carlton upon arrival via the Gold Coast trade; deal ran through the 2026 season (confirmed 'contracted for 2026' at time of October 2025 delisting, meaning one year remained). Exact length inferred as 3 years (2024-2026) since precise term was not publicly detailed.

events.name: Elijah Hollands
events.note: Delisted by Carlton with one year still remaining on his contract (through 2026), after being limited to 5 games in 2025 amid personal/off-field (mental health and alcohol) issues. Retained access to train-on opportunities over the pre-season.

events.name: Elijah Hollands
events.note: Re-signed by Carlton via the pre-season Supplemental Selection Period (SSP) after training on with the club following his October 2025 delisting, regaining an AFL list spot for the 2026 season. Contract length not publicly disclosed; SSP deals are typically single-season.

events.name: Joel Hamling
events.note: Signed with Western Bulldogs as a delisted free agent after three seasons on Geelong's list without a senior game.

events.name: Joel Hamling
events.note: Traded from Western Bulldogs to Fremantle (Freo sent picks 35, 43 & 61 for Hamling plus picks 40 & 63) on a contract understood to be three years, returning him to Western Australia after the Bulldogs' 2016 premiership win.

events.name: Joel Hamling
events.note: Signed a four-year extension on top of one year remaining on his existing deal, tying him to Fremantle to the end of 2023 (five years total at the time of signing, aged 25).

events.name: Joel Hamling
events.note: Left Fremantle (which had offered a one-year extension) and signed with Sydney as an unrestricted free agent, becoming his fourth AFL club.

events.name: Joel Hamling

A further extra-year deal to end of 2023 is evidenced (AFL.com.au: https://www.afl.com.au/news/758506/clubs-on-pre-agent-watch-former-no3-pick-paddy-dow-a-trade-target says he 'added an extra season' taking him to end of 2023; Zero Hanger 2 Oct 2022 says 'contracted for 2023') but no source gives its signing date, so it is not listed as a separate event.

events.name: Paddy Dow
events.note: Traded from Carlton to St Kilda in a four-club deal with Essendon and Western Bulldogs (St Kilda received Dow, pick 40 and a future third-round pick; Nick Coffield went to the Bulldogs). Deal agreed Tue 17 Oct 2023, confirmed by AFL Wed 18 Oct 2023. Club saints.com.au also covers it: https://www.saints.com.au/news/1453637/saints-welcome-dow. No source states the length/end of his initial St Kilda deal (appears to run 2024-2026), so no separate arrival signing event is listed.

events.name: Paddy Dow
events.note: One-year extension to end of 2026 as part of five St Kilda re-signings (Howard, Keeler, Stocker, Dow, O'Connell); Zero Hanger published 20 Aug 2025. Mirrored by https://www.saints.com.au/news/1868972/saints-lock-in-five-for-2026. Superseded by his delisting after 2026.

events.name: Paddy Dow
events.note: Delisted by St Kilda (with Isaac Keeler and Patrick Said), not offered a 2027 contract, at the end of his deal; 10 games for the Saints, none in 2025 or 2026. Zero Hanger confirms, published 27 Aug 2026: https://www.zerohanger.com/st-kilda-announces-2026-delistings-former-draft-pick-3-departs-181886/. Also club notice: https://www.saints.com.au/news/2113481/saints-farewell-keeler-dow-and-said. No later signing with another club found, so no event is current.

events.name: Archer Reid
events.note: Two-year extension to end of 2027, confirmed alongside Loch Rawlinson (West Coast club release 'Emerging Eagles sign on', 2 Sep 2024).

events.name: Archer Reid
events.reporter: The West Australian / West Coast Eagles
events.note: Three-year extension beyond his 2027 contract, through end of 2030; knocked back interest from Tasmania. Date from The West Australian report (3 Jul 2026); club page itself is undated. No retirement, delisting or trade found for 2026 off-season.

events.name: Alix Tauru
events.reporter: Zero Hanger (player profile); also Footywire, AFL.com.au
events.note: Original draft contract (never re-signed): pick 10 in the 2024 national draft, 20 Nov 2024 per AFLRATINGS. Date is the draft date, so it is estimated. Zero Hanger lists him contracted until 2027, Footywire shows 2027 as his final year, and AFL.com.au says one year remains on his deal. As of early Oct 2026 St Kilda had a reported four-year extension offer (to 2031) but no deal was signed. Gold Coast interest reportedly ended, and Twomey and Hayes said he wants to stay. No extension, trade, delisting or retirement found up to late Oct 2026. Web search budget ran out, so I could not check for a late-October signing.

events.name: Hugo Hall-Kahan
events.note: Delisted by Sydney at the end of 2023 after 18 months on the list (taken at pick 11 in the 2022 mid-season rookie draft, which is not listed as a separate event). The club said he would not be offered a new contract for 2024. Date taken from the club's embedded tweet of 8 Oct 2023. Wikipedia cites a Swans release of 9 Oct 2023. He then played VFL for Sandringham (2024) and Williamstown (2025 to mid-2026).

events.name: Hugo Hall-Kahan
events.note: Selected by Adelaide at pick 10 in the 2026 mid-season rookie draft, from Williamstown (VFL). The club article gives no contract length. The date comes from an embedded club tweet dated 26 May 2026. He debuted about 7 days later. The end year of 2026 is inferred: Footywire listed his contract as expiring in 2026, and the August extension added two years to reach 2028.

events.name: Hugo Hall-Kahan
events.note: Two-year extension to the end of 2028, announced with Zac Taylor and Finnbar Maley. The club page shows no date. The date of 4 Aug 2026 comes from the Wikipedia citation of this article. Zero Hanger also lists his contract as running until 2028.

events.name: Oscar Adams
events.note: Drafted by St Kilda at pick 51 in the 2021 national draft, played no senior games, and was delisted after the 2023 season (year confirmed by Draftguru, Wikipedia and Southern Eyre Voice; exact date not published, so it is estimated to the mid-October delisting period). He then played for Glenelg in the SANFL and was picked by Gold Coast at pick 7 in the 2025 mid-season rookie draft, which was his original deal there and is not listed here.

events.name: Oscar Adams
events.note: AFL.com.au post: 'Mature-age recruit Oscar Adams has been rewarded with another contract at Gold Coast for 2026.' The date comes from the post's ID timestamp (6 Aug 2025). The one-year length and the 2026 end are inferred from 'for 2026', and Footywire/Zero Hanger earlier listed him as out of contract at the end of 2026.

events.name: Oscar Adams
events.note: The club announced a further two seasons, through the end of 2028. The article is undated. It says Adams was the second Sun to re-sign in two days, after Jed Walter's extension to 2029. Walter's deal was reported as imminent on 12 Jul 2026 (Zero Hanger/SEN), so the date is estimated to mid-July 2026. Footywire (UFA end of 2028) and Zero Hanger (contracted until 2028) agree. No sign of any 2026 off-season delisting or trade.

events.name: Latrelle Pickett
events.note: Anchor deal: drafted by Melbourne at pick 12 in the 2025 AFL National Draft (first-round night, Wednesday 19 Nov 2025, per AFL.com.au and the Nine News draft URL). Never re-signed, traded or delisted. Contract length and end year are not published in any source found (Melbourne FC, AFL.com.au, Wikipedia, AFLRATINGS); left null. Debuted Round 1, 2026 and played 16 games. Web search quota ran out, so only direct page fetches were possible.

events.name: Jonty Faull
events.note: Two-year extension with Richmond through 2029, per AFLRATINGS contract news posted 18 Aug 2026. Drafted by Richmond at pick 14 in the 2024 draft (Wikipedia, ratings data). The page does not give the exact announcement date. No trade, delisting or retirement found. Web search budget ran out, so the club site and AFL.com.au could not be checked to confirm.

events.name: Saad El-Hawli

events.note: Delisted by Essendon at the end of the 2026 season, along with Matt Guelfi, Elijah Tsatas, Jade Gresham and Liam McMahon, after 17 AFL games over two years. Also https://www.sydneyswans.com.au/news/1025274/sydney-swans-welcome-peter-ladhams

events.name: Peter Ladhams
events.note: Swans club article says Ladhams signed 'a four year deal' with Sydney on arrival (2021 trade period). End year (2025) inferred from four years from 2022; consistent with later extension being a further two years to end of 2027.

events.name: Peter Ladhams
events.note: Two-year extension keeping him at Sydney until at least the end of 2027 (Leon Cameron: 'good reward for effort and consistency'). Exact day estimated.

events.name: Oliver Wiltshire

events.name: Shadeau Brain

events.name: Conor Stone
events.note: Two-year contract extension announced by GWS on 10 Oct 2024; end year inferred as 2026 from the two-year length. No earlier re-signing (between draft contract and this deal) was confirmed.

events.name: Conor Stone

events.name: Conor Stone

Article dated 21 Oct 2026 per Wikipedia's 2026 AFL draft reference; the article text gives no exact date. AFLRATINGS' 2026 retirements and delistings list also shows him as delisted (GWS). No redraft commitment was found, so no current deal.

events.name: Todd Marshall

events.name: Todd Marshall

Wikipedia lists him as a current Port Adelaide player (no. 4) through round 22 of 2026, and no delisting, trade or retirement was found, so this deal is still active.

events.name: Lincoln McCarthy

events.name: Lincoln McCarthy

events.name: Lincoln McCarthy

events.name: Lincoln McCarthy

events.name: Lincoln McCarthy

events.name: Lincoln McCarthy

events.name: Matthew Owies

Richmond received pick 14. The club's own article (westcoasteagles.com.au/news/1678610/bakers-lifelong-dream-comes-true) confirms the three-way trade but gives no date.

events.name: Matthew Owies
events.note: Joined West Coast on arrival via the trade. Contract length and end year were not disclosed in any source I could reach. No later extension was found, and he played 2025 and 2026 for West Coast.

events.name: Matthew Owies
events.note: AFLRATINGS records him as delisted by West Coast on 21 Oct 2026, and its page shows no current team. I could not find a club or AFL.com.au article to confirm this; the web search budget ran out. He has no active deal at end of 2026, so no event is current.

events.name: Sam Grlj
events.note: Drafted by Richmond at pick 8 in the 2025 national draft (20 Nov 2025); original draft contract is the anchor as he has not re-signed. Footywire lists him out of contract at the end of 2028. Draft date confirmed by SEN draft coverage dated 20 Nov 2025; no extension found.

events.name: Ashton Moir
events.note: Two-year extension, signed until at least the end of 2027. The Carlton article carries no date. 29 July 2025 comes from the Wikipedia citation of it and an embedded tweet dated 29 July 2025. Zero Hanger dates its extension story 30 July 2025 and BigFooty dates its report 2 August 2025. He was drafted at pick 29 in the 2023 AFL Draft and had two 2026 games to round 22. He was not among Carlton's September 2026 delistings (Zero Hanger, AFLRATINGS), and Footywire still lists him out of contract at the end of 2027.

events.name: Cooper Duff-Tytler

No extension, trade or delisting found; still on the West Coast list after 2026 (9 games).

events.name: Sam Cumming

Length is the 2026-2028 seasons, inferred from the end year.

events.name: Josh Dolan

Footywire also lists him out of contract at the end of 2028. He was drafted at pick 31 in the 2024 national draft, and that original draft deal is skipped. He is not in the Bulldogs' post-trade-period delisted, retired or traded-out lists (https://www.westernbulldogs.com.au/news/2151898/ins-and-outs-western-bulldogs-list-changes-after-the-trade-period), so the deal is still active.

events.name: Matthew Jefferson

events.name: Matthew Jefferson

events.name: Isaac Keeler
events.note: One-year extension announced with five other Saints (Webster, Byrnes, Stocker, McLennan, Heath), covering the 2025 season. Corroborated by NIT (nit.com.au, 9 Sep 2024) and the club's 'Six Saints sign on' (saints.com.au/news/1647426).

events.name: Isaac Keeler
events.note: Re-signed to remain until the end of 2026 as one of five Saints re-signings (Howard, Keeler, Stocker, Dow, O'Connell); length of one year is implied. Mirrored by saints.com.au 'Saints lock in five for 2026' (news/1868972).

events.name: Isaac Keeler

Club notice: saints.com.au/news/2113481/saints-farewell-keeler-dow-and-said; AFL.com.au also reported. As of 26-27 Oct 2026 he has not signed with another club (SEN 14 Oct reports an SA club will sign him; Port Adelaide has had talks and he is training with Port players, per Zero Hanger 26 Oct 2026; AFL.com.au ins and outs lists him only as a St Kilda delisted out). events.name: Zak Johnson
events.reporter: Essendon FC (official club site); dating corroborated by Zero Hanger
events.note: Essendon announced the 19-year-old half-back (pick 70, 2024 draft) re-signed for two more years, through the end of 2028. The club page carries no visible date. events.name: Campbell Gray

events.name: Matt Guelfi
